verdict.rationale: Linear's first-party Loops let users describe a recurring job in plain language and run it on a schedule or in response to workspace events, including changes to initiatives, projects and cycles. Documented actions include automatically updating a launch plan and posting a Slack message when a project's target date changes. That is a native trigger-and-action automation capability, supported by built-in auto-routing and labeling of incoming feedback and GitHub PR workflow automation. Missing for 10: a documented deterministic rule builder with explicit condition/action options (Loops are agent-driven), a full catalog of supported triggers and actions, and independent or hands-on corroboration that Loops work reliably.
